title: Sarga Four — verses 1–77
html:
Metre: drutavilambita (12 syllables per pada); verses 73–74 — toṭaka; verse 76 — śikhariṇī; verse 77 — vaṁśastha. Parallels: Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 12–13 (Nimai the teacher; the victory over Keshava Kashmiri); Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 16.

Contents of the passage:
- 1–4 — married life with Vishnupriya; the beauty of Gauranga.
- 5–20 — Gauranga as a teacher among His students (the verses are built on yamaka, the repetition of syllables; many passages are obscure).
- 21–24 — the journey to Gaya with Chandrashekhara Acharya.
- 25–49 — a poetic interlude: a lotus pond, sunset, night, morning, mountains and deer along the way (the story stands still; continuous yamaka).
- 50–55 — the river Chora: the fever, the cure with the water from the brahmanas' feet; Rajagiri (Rajagriha); the entry into Gaya.
- 56–61 — the meeting with Ishvara Puri; the initiation.
- 62–65 — the shraddha at Gaya (the Phalgu, Pretashila, Manasa); at the footprint of Vishnu — the first ecstasy.
- 66–68 — the impulse to go to Madhuvana (Vraja); a voice from the sky bids Him return.
- 69–75 — the return home, music; Shachi distributes gifts.
- 76–77 — the beginning of kirtana (the month of Magha).

Verse 1

अथ कृपारसवारिनिधीन्दुना
स्वजनमानसकैरवबन्धुना ।
दयितया सह तत्र विराजिता
निजगृहे जगृहे गृहमेधिता ॥१॥

atha kṛpā-rasa-vārinidhīndunā
sva-jana-mānasa-kairava-bandhunā |
dayitayā saha tatra virājitā
nija-gṛhe jagṛhe gṛhamedhitā ||1||

atha — then; kṛpā — of mercy; rasa — of the liquid; vārinidhi — of the ocean; indunā — by the moon; sva — of His own; jana — people; mānasa — of the hearts; kairava — of the white lilies; bandhunā — by the friend; dayitayā — the beloved; saha — with; tatra — there; virājitā — splendid; nija — in His own; gṛhe — in the house; jagṛhe — was accepted; gṛhamedhitā — the householder's life.

1Then, there in His own house, together with His beloved, He — the moon risen from the ocean of the nectar of mercy, the friend of the white lilies of His own people's hearts — accepted the splendid life of a householder.

Note. The moon rose from the churned Milk Ocean; the white lily (kairava) opens under the moon. A play of sounds: gṛhe jagṛhe gṛhamedhitā.

Verse 2

द्रुतसुवर्णसुवर्णरुचः शुचे-
र्मधुरकोमलशीतलविभ्रमः ।
श्रियमसौ मधुरामतिसुन्दरी-
मवपुषो वपुषोऽनुरुचाहरत् ॥२॥

druta-suvarṇa-suvarṇa-rucaḥ śucer
madhura-komala-śītala-vibhramaḥ |
śriyam asau madhurām ati-sundarīm
avapuṣo vapuṣo 'nurucāharat ||2||

druta — of molten; suvarṇa — gold; su — of beautiful; varṇa — colour; rucaḥ — [of the body] having the lustre; śuceḥ — of the pure; madhura — of sweet; komala — tender; śītala — cooling; vibhramaḥ — [He] of charm; śriyam — the beauty; asau — He; madhurām — sweet; ati — exceedingly; sundarīm — lovely; avapuṣaḥ — from the Bodiless One; vapuṣaḥ — of the body; anurucā — by the radiance; aharat — stole.

2He, full of sweet, tender and cooling charm, by the radiance of His pure body, which had the lustre of the beautiful colour of molten gold, stole the sweet and exceedingly lovely beauty of the Bodiless One.

Note. A play on words: avapuṣo vapuṣo, "from the Bodiless One … of the body". The Bodiless One is Kama, the god of love (cf. 3.30).

Verse 3

अमूमवेक्ष्य हृदा हृदयेशयः
सपदि निश्चितमित्थममन्यत ।
इममृते मम मन्मथता जनै-
रनुकथं नु कथं न हसिष्यते ॥३॥

amūm avekṣya hṛdā hṛdayeśayaḥ
sapadi niścitam ittham amanyata |
imam ṛte mama manmathatā janair
anukathaṁ nu kathaṁ na hasiṣyate ||3||

amūm — Him; avekṣya — having seen; hṛdā — with the heart; hṛdayeśayaḥ — "he who lies in the heart", the god of love; sapadi — at once; niścitam — firmly; ittham — thus; amanyata — thought; imam — Him; ṛte — beside; mama — my; manmathatā — fame as "the churner of minds"; janaiḥ — by people; anukatham — at every telling; nu — indeed; katham — how; na — not; hasiṣyate — will be laughed at.

3The god of love, seeing Him with his heart, at once firmly concluded: "Beside Him, how will my fame as 'the churner of minds' not be laughed at by people whenever it is spoken of?"

Note. Hṛdayeśaya, "he who lies in the heart", and manmatha, "churner of the mind", are both names of Kamadeva. The edition has amūm (feminine); the sense requires amum (masculine, "Him"). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 4

निजपदाब्जरसैरतिशीतलै-
र्जगदपूरयदात्तकृपारसः ।
य इह तत्कथने विरमन्त्यहो
तनुधरा नु धरासु वसन्ति ते ॥४॥

nija-padābja-rasair ati-śītalair
jagad apūrayad ātta-kṛpā-rasaḥ |
ya iha tat-kathane viramanty aho
tanu-dharā nu dharāsu vasanti te ||4||

nija — of His own; pada — of the feet; abja — of the lotuses; rasaiḥ — with the juices; ati — very; śītalaiḥ — cooling; jagat — the world; apūrayat — filled; ātta — having taken up; kṛpā — of mercy; rasaḥ — the taste; ye — who; iha — here; tat — about Him; kathane — from speaking; viramanti — cease; aho — ah; tanu — bodies; dharāḥ — bearing; nu — whether; dharāsu — on the earth; vasanti — live; te — they.

4Filled with the taste of mercy, He filled the world with the very cooling juices of His lotus feet. Ah, those here who cease from speaking of Him — do they [truly] live on the earth? They are mere bearers of bodies.

Note. A play on words: tanu-dharā, "body-bearers" — dharāsu, "on the earth".

Verse 5

अथ गुरुत्वमुपेत्य विकस्वरा-
म्बुजविलोलविलोचनखेलनैः ।
द्विजगणं समपाठयदेष य-
त्प्रतिभयातिभयाकुलितो गुरुः ॥५॥

atha gurutvam upetya vikasvarā-
mbuja-vilola-vilocana-khelanaiḥ |
dvija-gaṇaṁ samapāṭhayad eṣa yat
pratibhayāti-bhayākulito guruḥ ||5||

atha — then; gurutvam — the position of teacher; upetya — having assumed; vikasvara — of blossoming; ambuja — [like] lotuses; vilola — of restless; vilocana — of the eyes; khelanaiḥ — with the play; dvija — of brahmanas; gaṇam — the throng; samapāṭhayat — taught; eṣaḥ — He; yat — so that; pratibhayā — by [His] genius; ati — with great; bhaya — fear; ākulitaḥ — confounded; guruḥ — Guru [Brihaspati].

5Then, having become a teacher, He taught the throng of brahmanas with the play of His restless eyes, like blossoming lotuses — so that Guru himself, [the teacher of the gods,] was confounded by His genius, in great fear.

Note. A pun: pratibhayāti-bhaya, "by genius — great fear". Guru is both "teacher" and Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods and the standard of learning.

Verse 6

विविधशिष्यसदस्यपि राजतः
कनकगौरतनोर्मधुरद्युतेः ।
सुखवतः परिपाठयतोऽस्य सा
सुरुचिरा रुचिरास सुधारसम् ॥६॥

vividha-śiṣya-sadasy api rājataḥ
kanaka-gaura-tanor madhura-dyuteḥ |
sukhavataḥ paripāṭhayato 'sya sā
su-rucirā rucir āsa sudhā-rasam ||6||

vividha — of various; śiṣya — of students; sadasi — in the assembly; api — even; rājataḥ — [of Him] shining; kanaka — [like] gold; gaura — golden; tanoḥ — [of Him] whose body [is]; madhura — sweet; dyuteḥ — [of Him] whose effulgence [is]; sukhavataḥ — joyful; paripāṭhayataḥ — teaching; asya — of Him; sā — that; su — most; rucirā — lovely; ruciḥ — lustre; āsa — cast forth; sudhā — of nectar; rasam — the juice.

6As He — His body golden as gold, His effulgence sweet — shone even in the assembly of His various students and joyfully taught them, that most lovely lustre of His cast forth the juice of nectar.

Note. A play of sounds: su-rucirā rucir āsa. Āsa is taken as the perfect of as, "to throw, to cast forth", not as "was".

Verse 7

दशनरश्मिभिरच्छरदच्छदौ
स्नपयता सततं वदनेन्दुना ।
स्मितसुधामधुरेण महाप्रभु-
र्घनरुचा नवचारुरुचिर्बभौ ॥७॥

daśana-raśmibhir accha-radacchadau
snapayatā satataṁ vadanendunā |
smita-sudhā-madhureṇa mahāprabhur
ghana-rucā nava-cāru-rucir babhau ||7||

daśana — of the teeth; raśmibhiḥ — with the rays; accha — clear; radacchadau — the two lips; snapayatā — bathing; satatam — constantly; vadana — of the face; indunā — with the moon; smita — of the smile; sudhā — with the nectar; madhureṇa — sweet; mahāprabhuḥ — Mahaprabhu; ghana — with dense; rucā — lustre; nava — fresh; cāru — lovely; ruciḥ — [He] of radiance; babhau — shone.

7With the moon of His face, sweet with the nectar of His smile, constantly bathing His clear lips in the rays of His teeth, Mahaprabhu shone with dense lustre, His radiance fresh and lovely.

Note. The edition has घनरुधा; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads ghana-rucā, "with dense lustre", and we read so.

Verse 8

सकलशिष्यमुखानि महाप्रभोः
कलयतः ककुभः सततारुणाः ।
विदधिरे बहुविभ्रमयावलत्-
करुणयारुणया नयनश्रिया ॥८॥

sakala-śiṣya-mukhāni mahāprabhoḥ
kalayataḥ kakubhaḥ satatāruṇāḥ |
vidadhire bahu-vibhramayā valat-
karuṇayāruṇayā nayana-śriyā ||8||

sakala — of all; śiṣya — the students; mukhāni — the faces; mahāprabhoḥ — of Mahaprabhu; kalayataḥ — [of Him] looking upon; kakubhaḥ — the quarters; satata — ever; aruṇāḥ — red; vidadhire — were made; bahu — of much; vibhramayā — [full] of playfulness; valat — surging; karuṇayā — with compassion; aruṇayā — reddish; nayana — of the eyes; śriyā — by the beauty.

8As Mahaprabhu looked upon the faces of all His students, the quarters were made ever red by the reddish beauty of His eyes, full of playfulness and surging with compassion.

Note. A play of sounds: karuṇayā aruṇayā.

Verse 9

करतलेन गिरां गुरुविभ्रमै-
र्भ्रमवता स बभौ परितः स्फुरन् ।
कनकशैल इवोद्गतगैरिको-
दयलता लयताण्डवखेलनाम् ॥९॥

kara-talena girāṁ guru-vibhramair
bhramavatā sa babhau paritaḥ sphuran |
kanaka-śaila ivodgata-gairikodaya-latā-
laya-tāṇḍava-khelanām ||9||

kara — of the hand; talena — with the palm; girām — of speech; guru — with great; vibhramaiḥ — graces; bhramavatā — moving in circles; saḥ — He; babhau — shone; paritaḥ — all around; sphuran — flashing; kanaka — a golden; śailaḥ — mountain; iva — like; udgata — risen; gairika — of red ochre; udaya — emerging; latā — of the veins; laya — rhythmic; tāṇḍava — of the tandava dance; khelanām — [displaying] the play.

9With the palm of His hand moving in circles with the great graces of His speech, He shone, flashing all around, like a golden mountain [displaying] the play of a rhythmic tandava dance of risen, emerging veins of red ochre.

Note. The red palm against the golden body is like veins of red ochre (gairika) on a golden mountain. Tāṇḍava is a vigorous, rhythmic dance (the dance of Shiva). (?) The end of the verse is syntactically obscure; it is rendered according to the sense. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 10

अयमयं नु किमस्य कमस्य वा
किमयमर्थ उतस्विदयं त्विति ।
कलकलोऽस्य बभूव सुखाय स
त्रिचतुरैश्चतुरैः परितः कृतः ॥१०॥

ayam ayaṁ nu kim asya kam asya vā
kim ayam artha utasvid ayaṁ tv iti |
kala-kalo 'sya babhūva sukhāya sa
tri-caturaiś caturaiḥ paritaḥ kṛtaḥ ||10||

ayam — this; ayam — this; nu — is it; kim — what; asya — of this; kam — which; asya — of this; vā — or; kim — is it; ayam — this; arthaḥ — sense; utasvit — or perhaps; ayam — this; tu — indeed; iti — thus; kala-kalaḥ — the clamour; asya — to Him; babhūva — was; sukhāya — for delight; saḥ — that; tri — three; caturaiḥ — or four; caturaiḥ — by clever [students]; paritaḥ — all around; kṛtaḥ — raised.

10"Is it this? Or this? What is [the meaning] of this? Or which [word] of this? Is this the sense — or perhaps this?" — the clamour that three or four clever [students] raised all around Him was His delight.

Note. A lively scene: the students vie with one another over an interpretation. A play of sounds: tri-caturaiś caturaiḥ, "by three or four clever ones".

Verse 11

प्रभुमुखे युगपत्पतयालुभि-
र्विसृमरैरलिभिर्विदधे मुहुः ।
विततपक्षविधूननसक्षणै-
र्दिगबलागवलावलिविभ्रमा ॥११॥

prabhu-mukhe yugapat patayālubhir
visṛmarair alibhir vidadhe muhuḥ |
vitata-pakṣa-vidhūnana-sakṣaṇair
dig-abalā-gavalāvali-vibhramā ||11||

prabhu — of the Lord; mukhe — on the face; yugapat — all at once; patayālubhiḥ — alighting; visṛmaraiḥ — scattering; alibhiḥ — by bees; vidadhe — was produced; muhuḥ — again and again; vitata — of outspread; pakṣa — wings; vidhūnana — in the fluttering; sa-kṣaṇaiḥ — exultant; dik — of the quarters; abalā — for the maidens; gavala — of buffalo horn; āvali — of rows; vibhramā — the charm.

11Again and again the bees, now alighting all at once on the Lord's face, now scattering, exultant in the fluttering of their outspread wings, lent the maidens of the quarters the charm of rows of [ornaments black as] buffalo horn.

Note. The bees take the Lord's face for a lotus (cf. v. 12). In the edition the last pada reads dig-abalā abalāvali-vibhramāḥ; we read with the Gosvami edition (GGM) dig-abalā-gavalāvali-vibhramā: gavala is the horn of the wild buffalo, a byword for blackness.

Verse 12

किसलयं सलयं किमु वारुणं
सकमलं कमलं किमु वेत्यलिः ।
इह तदा हतदाक्ष्य इव प्रभोः
करदलं रदलङ्घनयाभजत् ॥१२॥

kisalayaṁ salayaṁ kimu vāruṇaṁ
sa-kamalaṁ kamalaṁ kimu vety aliḥ |
iha tadā hata-dākṣya iva prabhoḥ
kara-dalaṁ rada-laṅghanayābhajat ||12||

kisalayam — a young shoot; salayam — swaying; kimu — is it; vāruṇam — or red; sa — with; kamalam — water; kamalam — a lotus; kimu — is it; vā — or; iti — thus [wondering]; aliḥ — the bee; iha — here; tadā — then; hata — lost; dākṣyaḥ — [having] its cleverness; iva — as if; prabhoḥ — of the Lord; kara — of the hand; dalam — the petal; rada — of the teeth; laṅghanayā — with the touch (?); abhajat — resorted to.

12"Is it a swaying, red young shoot? Or is it a lotus in its water?" — so wondering, the bee, as if it had lost its wits, then fell upon the petal of the Lord's hand (?) with a touch of its teeth.

Note. A play of sounds: kisalayaṁ salayaṁ, sa-kamalaṁ kamalam (kam — "water"); vāruṇam is vā aruṇam, "or red". (?) Rada-laṅghanayā is obscure (literally "by the overstepping of the teeth"). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 13

नखसुधांशुसुधां शुचिमुक्षता
सुरुचिरेण चिरेण मधुव्रतः ।
करदलेन दलेन रुचाप्यभू-
द्धवलता वलता सुचिरोषितः ॥१३॥

nakha-sudhāṁśu-sudhāṁ śucim ukṣatā
su-rucireṇa cireṇa madhuvrataḥ |
kara-dalena dalena rucāpy abhūd
dhavalatā-valatā su-ciroṣitaḥ ||13||

nakha — of the nails; sudhāṁśu — of the moons; sudhām — the nectar; śucim — pure; ukṣatā — sprinkling; su — most; rucireṇa — lovely; cireṇa — long; madhuvrataḥ — the bee; kara — of the hand; dalena — by the petal; dalena — by the petal; rucā — by the lustre; api — also; abhūt — became; dhavala — from the white; latā — creepers; valatā — turned away; su — very; cira — long; uṣitaḥ — having dwelt.

13Because of the most lovely petal of His hand, which long sprinkled the pure nectar of the moons of His nails, and because of its lustre, the bee, which had long dwelt on the white creepers, turned away from them.

Note. The verse is built on yamaka, the repetition of identical syllables with different meanings: rucireṇa cireṇa, kara-dalena dalena, dhavalatā valatā. The translation follows the sense; many words in such verses cannot be analysed unambiguously. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 14

स परितः परिलक्ष्य धुरीणतां
मधुरिमा धुरि मानवतां श्रियाम् ।
भुवि हितं विहितं रचयन्सता-
मगमदागमदाक्ष्यममुष्य किम् ॥१४॥

sa paritaḥ parilakṣya dhurīṇatāṁ
madhurimā dhuri mānavatāṁ śriyām |
bhuvi hitaṁ vihitaṁ racayan satām
agamad āgama-dākṣyam amuṣya kim ||14||

saḥ — that; paritaḥ — on every side; parilakṣya — having perceived; dhurīṇatām — pre-eminence; madhurimā — sweetness; dhuri — at the head; mānavatām — of human beings; śriyām — of the beauties; bhuvi — on the earth; hitam — the good; vihitam — prescribed; racayan — arranging; satām — for the virtuous; agamat — came to know; āgama — in the scriptures; dākṣyam — the skill; amuṣya — His; kim — did not…? (?).

14(?) Sweetness, perceiving on every side His pre-eminence at the head of the beauties of human beings — did it not also come to know His skill in the scriptures, as He arranged on earth the prescribed good for the virtuous?

Note. (?) The verse is very obscure (yamaka: dhurīṇatāṁ … dhuri, agamad āgama). The translation is conjectural. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 15

प्रभुमुखेन्दुगलद्वचनामृतं
मृतजनस्य च जीवितदायि तत् ।
श्रुतिपथेन निपीय चिरेण ते
मुदमिता दमिताखिलकल्मषाः ॥१५॥

prabhu-mukhendu-galad-vacanāmṛtaṁ
mṛta-janasya ca jīvita-dāyi tat |
śruti-pathena nipīya cireṇa te
mudam itā damitākhila-kalmaṣāḥ ||15||

prabhu — of the Lord; mukha — of the face; indu — from the moon; galat — flowing; vacana — of words; amṛtam — the nectar; mṛta — to a dead; janasya — person; ca — even; jīvita — life; dāyi — giving; tat — that; śruti — of hearing; pathena — by the path; nipīya — having drunk; cireṇa — long; te — they; mudam — joy; itāḥ — attained; damita — subdued; akhila — all; kalmaṣāḥ — [they whose] sins [were].

15Having long drunk through the path of their ears the nectar of words flowing from the moon of the Lord's face — a nectar that gives life even to the dead — they, all their sins subdued, attained joy.

Note. A play of sounds: mudam itā damitā.

Verse 16

धवलपक्षसपक्षरुगंशुकः
शुकचञ्चुरुचं चुलुकीकृताम् ।
मधुरयोर्नु दधेऽधरयोरसौ
मधुरयोर्यदयं परिजृम्भते ॥१६॥

dhavala-pakṣa-sapakṣa-rug-aṁśukaḥ
śuka-cañcu-rucaṁ culukī-kṛtām |
madhurayor nu dadhe 'dharayor asau
madhurayor yad ayaṁ parijṛmbhate ||16||

dhavala — of the bright; pakṣa — fortnight; sapakṣa — like; ruk — [whose] lustre [is]; aṁśukaḥ — [He whose] garment [is]; śuka — of the parrot; cañcu — of the beak; rucam — the beauty; culukī — a mouthful; kṛtām — made into; madhurayoḥ — in the sweet; nu — did not…?; dadhe — held; adharayoḥ — in the lips; asau — He; madhurayoḥ — over the sweet [lips]; yat — since; ayam — it; parijṛmbhate — spreads.

16His garment had the lustre of the bright fortnight of the moon. Did He not take the beauty of the parrot's beak in a single sip and hold it in His sweet lips? — for it spreads over those sweet [lips].

Note. The edition gives nudadhe and madhu-rayo ("a stream of honey"); we read with the Gosvami edition (GGM) nu dadhe and madhurayor: the Lord's lips are red like a parrot's beak.

Verse 17
